sources: Israel Central Elections Committee (poll mechanics); Gadi Eisenkot X post 06:29 Israel time; Netanyahu Channel 14 interview Oct 26; Trump social post Oct 26; Japan Times / AFP / Dawn Oct 27 reporting
fault_line: Accountability for October 7 vs 'only Netanyahu can finish the job on Iran' -- does the election change the Iran war, or does the war decide the election?

sections.what_happened: On election morning, Eisenkot posted at 06:29 'Remember this hour when you go to vote... to replace the government of October 7th'; Netanyahu campaigned on Channel 14 that only removing Iran's 'fanatical, zealous regime' secures Israel's future and that 'Gadi Eisenkot will not strike Iran'; Trump posted 'Vote for Bibi Netanyahu... we have to finish the job that we started!'; final polls show Netanyahu's bloc and Eisenkot's opposition bloc each near 53 seats, short of the 61 needed; 7,331,981 eligible voters, 12,018 stations, polls 07:00-22:00 Israel time.
sections.what_verified: Polls open, voter/station counts, tight race and 61-seat threshold confirmed across AFP (via Khaleej Times), Japan Times and Dawn; Eisenkot 06:29 quote carried by Republic World/Devdiscourse (ANI syndication, no declared registry tier) and consistent with the opposition's October 7-accountability campaign line; Netanyahu Channel 14 lines via Malay Mail (AFP) Oct 27; Trump endorsement quote via Japan Times Oct 27.
sections.what_disputed: Netanyahu's office rejected the CNN pre-election strike-push reporting as 'fake news' (covered 0900-01, still HOLD); Defence Minister Israel Katz called reports of an army-political gap 'entirely baseless and false'; Netanyahu denies the Channel 12 Zamir-clash report as 'rubbish'. No exit poll or result exists yet -- any 'win/loss' framing before 22:00 Israel time would be fabrication.
sections.why_matters: Election day, but the ballot is really about the Iran war: 7.33 million voters, neither bloc at 61, and both campaigns fought their last round on Iran -- Eisenkot's 06:29 October 7 appeal vs Netanyahu's annihilation warning and Trump's 'finish the job' endorsement.
sections.context: Background: ELECTION-DAY UPDATE -- Israel votes: Eisenkot's 06:29 October 7 appeal, Netanyahu's 'finish the job' / annihilation line, Trump endorsement; coalition math blocks either bloc

totw_analysis: Our read: Election day, but the ballot is really about the Iran war: 7.33 million voters, neither bloc at 61, and both campaigns fought their last round on Iran -- Eisenkot's 06:29 October 7 appeal vs Netanyahu's annihilation warning and Trump's 'finish the job' endorsement. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Accountability for October 7 vs 'only Netanyahu can finish the job on Iran' -- does the election change the Iran war, or does the war decide the election?
